stations.body: Leadership visit From November 3 to November 6, we embarked on a remarkable week dedicated to learning, growth, and meaningful connection. Curated training sessions sparked meaningful discussions and equipped participants with practical strategies for giving and receiving feedback, strengthening stakeholder relationships, and writing with impact. stations.title: Behind-the-scenes!
stations.body:
Behind-the-scenes!
Latest creative moves, big ideas, and tiny tweaks Crafting proposals is an art that we are transforming into science. We don’t just follow best practices; we invent them to make the proposal creation journey smarter, more efficient, and dare we say…fun.
From small but mighty fixes to fresh design hacks, we have been tackling those little ‘proposal quirks’ one by one. Here, we dish out the secret sauce behind turning ‘good’ into ‘marvelous’—from clever content tips, and design tricks to workflow improvement that make our work shine. Think of it as our very own lab where we’re brewing up solutions for every little proposal pickle that pops up. So, buckle in, grab your imagination hats, and get ready to see how we’re making proposals sparkle one genius tweak at a time!

Latest tips:
• Using Adobe Color checker for color accessibility: Aastha
• Must know After Effects shortcuts to make your life easy: Praful
• Horizon feedback: Sateesh
• Solution for ‘PPT repair’ issue for Mac users: Simon and Prasad
• Reviving author names in comments on PowerPoint: Anindya

stations.title: Calling all Proposal Ninjas
stations.body:
Calling all Proposal Ninjas Calling all creative thinkers and problem solvers! We’re on the lookout for bright ideas that can take our proposal game to the next level. If you have come up with a clever hack, a time-saving process, or even a unique design sprinkle that’s made a difference in our proposals, we want to hear about it! And wait… if you are battling “Is-my-idea-good-enough” syndrome, then please remember— sometimes, it’s the tiniest tweak that makes the biggest impact!
Please contact the USI Pursuit COE Innovate to Evolve team member ( Aastha , Vinnu , Deepak , Ben , Sephin and Bharti ) to contribute.

stations.title: What we did
stations.body:
Leadership visit From November 3 to November 6, we embarked on a remarkable week dedicated to learning, growth, and meaningful connection. Curated training sessions sparked meaningful discussions and equipped participants with practical strategies for giving and receiving feedback, strengthening stakeholder relationships, and writing with impact. Lesli Hamilton, Annabell Lepe, Kandace Gallant, Vineet Arora, Rajat Mishra, and Ripunjay (RJ) Nandikonda facilitated workshops on ‘Culture of Feedback,’ ‘Master Delivery,’ and ‘Smart Brevity.’ These sessions provided attendees with valuable and actionable insights to elevate their impact and drive success together.

Now, let’s hear directly from our participants about their experiences:

“Effective communication isn’t about saying more—it’s about focusing on what matters most. In our recent training, I learned the value of the ‘10% effective message’: distilling feedback to the few most actionable and relevant insights, rather than overwhelming clients with excessive detail.”
—
Rashmi Pandey, pursuit researcher “The sessions broadened my perspective, deepening my understanding of how a culture of collaboration, meaningful content, and constructive feedback drives growth and continuous improvement.”
—Jyoshna Sree, designer, Pursuit Design Studio

We had concurrent sessions with the leaders, aligned to our work deliverables. This provided us with a bird's-eye view of work that includes stitching up the storytelling elements, understanding smart brevity closely, and placing the 10% messaging to make it memorable.”
—Ayan Gupta, Tax pursuit manager “I really connected with the idea that ‘brevity is confidence’ — it reminded me to communicate with more clarity and impact. The concept of crafting my 10% also stood out, pushing me to focus on what truly adds value and makes my message unique.”
—Mayoura Chatta, Audit pursuit manager
